name: norvel
author: music-rhythm-and-dance agent
description:
norvel v2 (direction: music, rhythm and dance) - A KICK ROW AND A SNARE ROW: THE HOLES THE SNARE
FILLS EXACTLY. PRIVATE; never shown to players.

CLUE = "<kick>/<n>". <kick> is one drum row of 28-48 steps (always a multiple of 4) over "x" (a hit)
and "." (a rest); it starts and ends with a hit and has G = 7..10 maximal HOLES (maximal runs of
"."). Within one clue every hole is w or w+1 steps wide for a base width w in 2..4, so there are no
1-step holes and exactly two hole widths. n = 2..8 with G - n = 2..6, so n is never the number of
holes (the complement of the clue is always wrong), and generate() also refuses n equal to the
number of kick runs, the number of kick hits, the longest hole, the number of longest holes, the
number of shortest holes, the number of bars or the number of 3-hit kick runs: n cannot be read off
the kick row alone.

SOLUTION = a two-line drum-machine picture. The scorer deletes every character that is not "x" or
".", drops empty lines, and requires EXACTLY TWO rows, the same length, with the FIRST row equal to
the clue row. Labels ("kick"/"snare", "bd"/"sn", "K"/"S", "boom"/"bap", ...), bar lines "|", a
"|1234|1234|" beat header, spaces, tabs, blank lines and CRLF are all free - the grader reads only
the x/. skeleton.
THE RULE (unchanged from v1): exactly n of the maximal runs of "x" in the SECOND row have exactly
the same span (same first step AND same last step) as a hole of the clue row. "The snare fills n of
the kick's holes exactly - no more, no less."

WHAT CHANGED IN v2 (softening by salience only - DESIGN_LOOP lever 9; the rule and the scorer's
predicate are identical):
 (a) THE HAT ROW IS GONE. v1 was three rows; both v1 players read the three voices as one texture,
     fitted a groove-shaped sampler and never once compared a snare run with a kick hole. A third
     row cannot be made harmless here: any fixed tick (every 2nd or 4th step) lands inside counted
     holes for an arbitrary kick row, which is exactly the competition DESIGN_LOOP (c) forbids.
     Two rows also make the picture the thing the rule is about: kick against snare.
 (b) THE SNARE ROW CARRIES NOTHING BUT ITS RUNS. v1's solve() sprayed 5-20 % filler on kick hits
     and 35-50 % on the hat; v2 emits the n exact fills, at most three planted near-misses and
     silence. Every snare run in a demo is therefore one of the four cases: an exact fill, a run
     too short inside a hole, a run that covers a hole and spills over a kick hit, or a run as long
     as a hole in the wrong place. At high n the picture is a visible zipper (the snare's runs
     interlock with the kick's gaps); at low n it is four or five isolated runs, two of which fit a
     gap exactly.
 (c) THE CLUES ARE BIGGER AND MORE DISPERSED: G = 7..10 (was 4..8), n = 2..8 (was 2..5), G - n =
     2..6 (was 1..4), two hole widths per clue drawn from a base 2..4 (was 1..5). This is what
     drops the blind groove sampler from 28 % to 17 % (below) - with 7-10 holes and n/G spread over
     0.25..0.8 there is no single rest-density that lands on "exactly n" for most clues.

INTENDED DISCOVERY PATH. (a) it is a drum grid and the top line is the clue - round 1, one demo;
(b) the snare plays in the kick's gaps - the picture says it out loud; (c) not every gap and not
every run: count them, it is n; (d) EXACTLY, not "inside" and not "over" - forced by the near-miss
in every demo. Kid sentence from one demo: "the snare fills up five of the kick's gaps exactly - it
starts the moment the kick stops and stops the moment the kick comes back - and the other gaps it
either misses or plays over."

DEMO GUARANTEES (measured, 1200 demos): a run too short inside a hole 100 %; a run that covers a
whole hole and spills over a kick hit 100 %; a non-fill run exactly as long as some hole 100 %
(1.7 per demo); a run sitting on kick hits away from every hole 39 %; a hole left silent 55 %;
the longest fill is as wide as the widest hole 100 %. 17 rival counters (runs, hits, holes touched,
holes covered, holes silent, runs inside/containing/as-long-as a hole, runs flush to a hole's start
or end, unison hits, runs touching a kick hit, distinct run lengths, longest run, bars with a hit,
holes with one hit) are checked per demo: all 17 differ from n on 99.8 % of demos, and on the
remaining 0.2 % (where no picture satisfying all of them exists) the six core rivals still do.

WITNESS TABLE (1200 fresh clues; v1 number in brackets where it differs)
  the true rule (solve)                                      100.00 %
  empty / junk / clue echoed / 4000 chars / clue row twice      0.00 %
  clue row + an empty or a full row                             0.00 %
  the v1 three-row format                                       0.00 %
  a random snare row, density 0.2 -> 0.8                   0.00-0.61 %
  GROOVE SAMPLER (kick-rest bias) p=0.78/0.89/0.80/0.85/0.95  13.9-17.3 %   [v1: 28.1 %, and the
      v1 players scored 27 % and 36 % with exactly this]
  groove sampler, density tuned per clue so E[fills]=n         29.03 %   [v1: 37.8 %] - this one
      already needs the whole insight (compute the holes, aim at n) and is a stupid way to use it
  COMPLEMENT (fill every hole)                                  0.00 %   (closed by n < G)
  complement minus one hole                                     0.00 %   (closed by G - n >= 2)
  complement minus two / three holes                     24.50 / 16.92 %
  "always fill exactly k holes", k = 2..6                  12.0-22.4 %
  fill the n longest / n shortest holes exactly               100.00 %   (= the rule; which holes
      never matters)
  graft an old answer's snare row under the new kick row        3.33 %
  demo replay on the next clue / one fixed answer         0.00 / 0.08 %
  n holes get a random run INSIDE (the loose reading)           3.08 %
  n holes: run flush to the hole's left edge                    2.94 %
  n holes get ONE snare hit / n holes covered with a spill      0.00 %
  n unison hits on the kick / exactly n snare runs anywhere     0.00 %
  right rule but n-1 / n+1 holes, or the rows swapped           0.00 %
Read it as a gradient: 0 % (no idea) -> 0.6 % (the format only) -> 3 % (runs in the gaps, the loose
reading) -> 12-25 % (the exact match found, the meaning of n missed: "fill k of them", "all but
two") -> ~17 % for the best insight-free groove -> 100 % (the rule). FOOTHOLD (DESIGN_LOOP lever 7):
the natural first probe after one demo - "the snare plays through the kick's gaps" at any density -
pays 16-18 %, so nobody concludes the grader is exact-match; and it is a plateau, not a ladder,
because no amount of density tuning gets past ~18 % without counting.

FAIRNESS. Over a family of 62 "count a relation in the picture" counters the demos leave
2.7 -> 1.3 -> 1.0 survivors after 1..3 demos and the last survivor is the true rule in 15/15 trials.
Two demos pin the rule for anyone who enumerates snare-run/kick-hole relations at all; all the
difficulty is in looking there, which is what v2's picture is built to make unavoidable.

VALIDATION. quickcheck --seeds 200: OK, no warnings. score 269/512, solve 4448/5000, generate 1180.
solve() scores 1 on 1500/1500 fresh clues (5.0 ms mean, 248 ms worst); generate deterministic on
4000 seeds, 0.030 ms mean / 0.14 ms worst, clue <= 50 chars. Scorer: 0 raises, 0 non-binary and 0
false positives on 8800 junk strings (worst 0.19 ms); 0 disagreements with an independent
re-implementation on 12000 mutated answers. Leniency 100 % (bare rows, bar lines, labels, header,
blank lines, tabs, CRLF, stray spaces); strictness 0 % (rows swapped, snare only, three rows, one
wrong character in the kick row, snare shifted by one, snare emptied, all on one line; snare
reversed 2.2 % = palindromic coincidence).

LEVERS. Too easy (the risk after v2): count only holes >= 3 steps wide; require the fills to be
non-adjacent; make G - n always 2 or 3 so the count is nearly the complement and the near-misses
carry all the information. Too hard: guarantee two silent holes per demo; put the number of holes
in the clue as a second field; shrink G back to 5..7.
